orgDesign.companyProfile: Software company modeled on Infotopics | Apps for Tableau (Lage Doelen 2, Hardenberg, NL and 25 Watling Street, London, UK): about 30 employees building 30+ premium extensions for Tableau, Power BI and Looker Studio, used by 600+ organisations in 150+ countries and sold directly and through 32 partner firms. Founded in 2018 by Merlijn Buit (CTO, Tableau Visionary) and Richard van Wijk (CEO) out of Infotopics, a Tableau Gold Partner since 2011; the first product ShowMeMore was shown in the Tableau Conference 2018 keynote and the team won the Tableau Innovative Solution Award that year. Revenue comes from Free, Professional and Enterprise subscriptions per organisation, priced by active dashboard users (anonymous unique tokens over a rolling 12 months) and deployment model (SaaS-hosted or self-hosted Enterprise); WriteBackExtreme and MailScheduler are Enterprise-only. Since the Vortex Capital Partners buyout of 26 March 2026 the company is funded to accelerate product development and international presence, expand the portfolio with AI functionality and make selective strategic acquisitions; the two founders continue to lead.
orgDesign.operatingModel: With about 30 people the organisation is deliberately flat: three groups, each led by a working founder or lead rather than a management layer, and ten teams of 2-4 people who own their bricks end to end (product, build, release, run and second-line support). Four stream-aligned extension product teams own the lifecycle Build -> Use -> Distribute for their product families (write-back and planning, tables and discovery, visual storytelling, distribution and adoption). Two platform teams provide what every extension shares: the extension runtime (framework, data connector, multi-platform adapters) and the licensing, deployment and identity stack that turns an extension into a sellable, installable, safelisted product. Two enabling teams embed AI into the extensions and carry ISO 27001, penetration testing and vendor-assessment evidence. The go-to-market group runs the website, trials, gallery and the 32-firm partner network, and the support, documentation and customer-success motion. Because the product lives inside somebody else's platform, extension-runtime and deployment-and-licensing are explicit x-as-a-service dependencies of every product team, and Tableau, Microsoft and Google release cycles set much of the roadmap cadence. The Vortex thesis (AI in the product, international growth through partners, buy-and-build) is expressed through ai-enablement, growth-and-partners and a runtime built so acquired extensions can be plugged in. Every team is steward of the data assets its bricks create; in Enterprise deployments write-back records, comments and audit logs stay in the customer's own databases and the vendor never sees them.
